The '''2009–10 Ligue 1 season''' was the 72nd since its establishment. [[FC Girondins de Bordeaux|Bordeaux]] were the [[2008–09 Ligue 1|defending champions]]. The fixtures were announced on 5 June 2009, and play commenced on 8 August and ended on 15 May 2010.<ref>{{cite news|title=Les calendriers 2009/2010 de Ligue 1 et Ligue 2 dévoilés |url=http://www.lfp.fr/actualiteLFP/lireArticle.asp?idArticle=13392 |work=Ligue de Football Professionel |publisher=lfp.fr |date=5 June 2009 |access-date=5 June 2009 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090608050118/http://www.lfp.fr/actualiteLFP/lireArticle.asp?idArticle=13392 |archive-date=8 June 2009 }}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Le calendrier général de la saison 2009/2010 |url=http://www.lfp.fr/communique/lireArticle.asp?idArticle=12606 |work=Ligue de Football Professionel |publisher=lfp.fr |date=5 June 2009 |access-date=5 June 2009 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090505060436/http://www.lfp.fr/communique/lireArticle.asp?idArticle=12606 |archive-date=5 May 2009 }}</ref> There were three promoted teams from [[2008–09 Ligue 2|Ligue 2]], replacing the three teams that were relegated from Ligue 1 following the [[2008–09 Ligue 1|2008–09 season]]. A total of 20 teams competed in the league with three clubs suffering relegation to the second division, [[Ligue 2]]. All clubs that secured Ligue 1 status for this season were subject to approval by the [[Direction Nationale du Contrôle de Gestion|DNCG]] before becoming eligible to participate.<ref name=bye>The DNGC is responsible for overseeing the legal and financial accounts of professional and amateur football clubs in France. If clubs operating in the football leagues of France did not meet the DNGC's expectations, they could face sanctions, such as relegation.</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Actualités DNCG |url=http://www.lfp.fr/dncg/ |work=LFP |publisher=Ligue de Football Professionnel |date=26 May 2009 |access-date=26 May 2009 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090603073237/http://www.lfp.fr/dncg/ |archive-date=3 June 2009 }}</ref> In addition, German [[Sportswear (activewear)|sportswear]] company [[Puma AG|Puma]] became the official provider of match balls for the season after agreeing to a long term [[partnership]] with the [[Ligue de Football Professionnel]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Les ballons officiels Ligue 1 – Ligue 2 révélés |url=http://www.lfp.fr/actualiteLFP/lireArticle.asp?idArticle=13384 |work=LFP |publisher=Ligue de Football Professionnel |date=5 June 2009 |access-date=5 June 2009 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090607073426/http://www.lfp.fr/actualiteLFP/lireArticle.asp?idArticle=13384 |archive-date=7 June 2009 }}</ref>

The season began on 8 August 2009 under a new format with 16 clubs beginning play simultaneously followed by 4 clubs competing the following day. Under the new format, the showcase match of the opening week will contest the winners of the league the previous season and the winners of the second division the previous season. In the match this year, [[2008–09 Ligue 1|defending champions]] [[FC Girondins de Bordeaux|Bordeaux]] defeating [[2008–09 Ligue 2|second division champions]] [[RC Lens|Lens]] 4–1 at the [[Stade Chaban-Delmas]].

On 5 May 2010, [[Olympique de Marseille|Marseille]] defeated [[Stade Rennais F.C.|Rennes]] 3–1 to claim their 9th Ligue 1 title and their first since the [[1991–92 Division 1|1991–92 season]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=271425&cc=5739|archive-url=https://archive.today/20120716075853/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report?id=271425&cc=5739|url-status=dead|archive-date=16 July 2012|title=Marseille 3–1 Stade Rennes|date=5 May 2010|work=[[ESPNsoccernet]]|publisher=[[ESPN]]|access-date=5 May 2010}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.lfp.fr/ligue1/lireArticle.asp?idArticle=16258 |title=L'OM champion de France ! |date=5 May 2010 |work=[[Ligue 1]] |publisher=[[Ligue de Football Professionnel]] |access-date=5 May 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100509150024/http://www.lfp.fr/ligue1/lireArticle.asp?idArticle=16258 |archive-date=9 May 2010}}</ref> Because of their [[Coupe de la Ligue]] title, Marseille claimed the [[double (association football)|league and league cup double]]. It is the second straight season a club has won the league and league cup double with [[FC Girondins de Bordeaux|Bordeaux]] achieving it last season.

(8 August 2009).<ref>{{cite news |title=Grenoble v. Montpellier Match Report |url=http://www.lfp.fr/ligue1/feuilleMatch.asp?saison=2009/2010&code_evt=D1&num_ordre=1&code_jr_tr=J32 |publisher=LFP |date=10 April 2010 |access-date=11 April 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100412142334/http://www.lfp.fr/ligue1/feuilleMatch.asp?saison=2009%2F2010&code_evt=D1&num_ordre=1&code_jr_tr=J32 |archive-date=12 April 2010 |url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Miscellaneous===
*Longest second half injury time: '''5 minutes and 56 seconds''' – [[RC Lens|Lens]] against [[Lille OSC|Lille]] (20 September 2009).
*On 9 August 2009, [[FC Girondins de Bordeaux|Bordeaux]] established a record for most consecutive league wins with 12 surpassing [[Lille OSC|Lille]] who won 11 consecutive matches in 1949, winning their last four games of the [[1948–49 French football Division 1|1948–49 season]] and their first seven in the [[1949–50 French football Division 1|1949–50 season]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Avec 12 victoires consécutives, Bordeaux établit un nouveau record |url=http://www.ladepeche.fr/article/2009/08/09/651965-Avec-12-victoires-consecutives-Bordeaux-etablit-un-nouveau-record.html|publisher=La Dépêche |date=9 August 2009 |access-date=25 October 2009 }}</ref> Bordeaux's streak began during the [[2008–09 Ligue 1|2008–09 season]] on 14 March 2009 following a 2–1 victory over [[OGC Nice|Nice]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Bordeaux v. Nice Match Report |url=http://www.lfp.fr/ligue1/feuilleMatch.asp?saison=2008/2009&code_evt=&code_jr_tr=J28&num_ordre=1&no_groupe=0 |publisher=LFP |date=14 March 2009 |access-date=9 August 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090501121018/http://www.lfp.fr/ligue1/feuilleMatch.asp?saison=2008%2F2009&code_evt=&code_jr_tr=J28&num_ordre=1&no_groupe=0 |archive-date=1 May 2009 |url-status=dead}}</ref> The club broke the record on the opening match day of this season defeating [[RC Lens|Lens]] 4–1.<ref>{{cite news |title=Bordeaux v. Lens Match Report |url=http://www.lfp.fr/ligue1/feuilleMatch.asp?saison=2009/2010&code_evt=D1&num_ordre=2&code_jr_tr=J01 |publisher=LFP |date=9 August 2009 |access-date=9 August 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090812041835/http://www.lfp.fr/ligue1/feuilleMatch.asp?saison=2009%2F2010&code_evt=D1&num_ordre=2&code_jr_tr=J01 |archive-date=12 August 2009 |url-status=dead}}</ref> The record lasted for 14 matches before coming to an end on 30 August following the club's 0–0 draw with [[Olympique de Marseille|Marseille]].
*On 31 October 2009, [[Grenoble Foot 38|Grenoble]] set a record for most consecutive losses in [[French football]] following the club's eleven straight league defeat, an 0–2 loss to [[Lille OSC|Lille]]. The previous record of ten straight defeats, held by [[FC Sète|Sète]], had been intact since 1947. The losing streak came to an end the following week, on 7 November, following the club's 0–0 draw with [[AS Monaco FC|Monaco]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Grenoble à 1 match du record européen de défaites |url=http://www.liberation.fr/sports/0101601692-foot-grenoble-a-1-match-du-record-europeen-de-defaites|publisher=Liberation|date=7 November 2009 |access-date=7 November 2009 }}</ref>
